chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ubayd al-Khayyat, from Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If a man has a thousand dirhams with him, and he has nothing else, then he buys sugar with it, he would not be considered extravagant.

key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: Dirham, a silver coin used as currency

ai.seo_question: What constitutes financial extravagance (israf) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that 'israf' (extravagance) is not defined by the total depletion of one's wealth but by the nature of the expenditure and context. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that purchasing a single commodity, even with all available funds, is permissible unless it leads to waste or neglect of obligatory duties, distinguishing mere high spending from true wastefulness. This hadith is often cited in discussions on personal finance and the permissibility of luxury goods in Islamic law.
